listening:No hi-fi bar inside the walls.name: No hi-fi bar inside the walls
listening:No hi-fi bar inside the walls.teaser: No listening bar, no audiophile counter: Dubrovnik's best music is sung live, in stone squares and halls
listening:No hi-fi bar inside the walls.story: We went looking for a listening bar in Dubrovnik, the kind of room with a serious sound system, a wall of records and a bartender who lets the side play out. In October 2026 we found none, inside the walls or out. The nearest thing is a habit, not a venue: the Dubrovnik 33/45 association has run monthly record nights with Love Bar, up the hill from the Gruž harbourfront, and in December 2025 the two staged the first Dubrovnik Vinyl DJ Festival there with fourteen local selectors playing only records. No 2026 edition was announced. What the city does have is voices: klapa and the lijerica, live, in summer.
listening:No hi-fi bar inside the walls.why: Spend the evening on live klapa or the Linđo in summer; in winter, bring your own headphones.
facts: Nothing to visit: no hi-fi or listening bar was found in Dubrovnik in October 2026. The 2025 Vinyl DJ Festival at Love Bar in Gruž was a one-off, with no 2026 date announced
The Linđo at Lazareti and live klapa in the Old Town, both summer only, each with its own card in this section; then the records of Oliver Dragojević, Gibonni and Klapa Cambi for the galley

listening:Linđo at Lazareti.name: Linđo at Lazareti
listening:Linđo at Lazareti.teaser: One bowed lyre, a stamping foot and a ring of Konavle dancers under the old quarantine vaults
listening:Linđo at Lazareti.story: The lijerica is a small pear-shaped fiddle with three strings, held upright on the knee and bowed. Its player sits in the middle of the floor and beats time with his foot on the stone while a caller shouts the figures in rhyme, and the dancers around him turn, swap partners, speed up and stop on command. That is the Linđo, the dance of the Konavle valley and the Dubrovnik coast. The Linđo Folklore Ensemble, founded in the mid-1960s, keeps it alive and stages it on summer nights in the Lazareti, the long row of stone halls just past the Ploče Gate, in full Konavle costume.
listening:Linđo at Lazareti.why: Watch the lijerica player's right foot: the whole dance hangs on that beat.
facts: Summer only, about mid-May to early October; the 2026 run was listed for Tuesdays and Fridays at 21:30 (Oct 2026), and the season is now over. Check the 2027 days with the tourist board
Lazareti, Ul. Frana Supila, just outside the Ploče Gate; Lazareti's own story is on its Culture card. The ensemble also plays one-off dates for the Summer Festival, at Revelin in July 2026
Ticketed; we found no 2026 price, so ask at the tourist office
The Linđo is often called UNESCO-listed: it is not on the list itself. Easter in the Konavle villages, with the dance in churchyards, is on the calendar

listening:Klapa in the churches.name: Klapa, live in the Old Town
listening:Klapa in the churches.teaser: Five or six men, no instruments, a semicircle on the stones and chords that ring off the palace walls
listening:Klapa in the churches.story: Klapa is Dalmatian multipart singing without instruments, a small group of mostly male voices in a close half-ring, the first tenor leading; UNESCO inscribed it in 2012. In Dubrovnik the summer klapa is free and outdoors. Each June to mid-September the city and the tourist board run Ulicama našeg grada, Through the Streets of Our City, with the local groups taking turns: in 2025 Klapa Kaše sang at ten at night in front of the Rector's Palace, Klapa Subrenum by the Large Onofrio Fountain, Klapa Ragusavecchia on the Lapad promenade. The church acoustics come in spring, when the Aklapela festival has held closing concerts in St Dominic's and the cathedral.
listening:Klapa in the churches.why: Hear a Dubrovnik group in the open at night, not a recording in a restaurant; Klapa Kaše are the city's own.
facts: June to mid-September, late evening, usually 21:30 or 22:00; nothing regular runs in late October or winter. The Aklapela klapa festival has been held in April in past years
In front of the Rector's Palace, along Stradun, by the Large Onofrio Fountain, and on the Lapad Bay promenade; the spot changes nightly
The summer street programme is open-air and public; we found no ticket price listed (Oct 2026). The EUR 10-15 church concerts of the old guide could not be found again
Check the tourist board calendar on the day for which klapa sings where; the Omiš Festival, the national contest, has its own card under the calendar

listening:Oliver Dragojević.name: Oliver Dragojević
listening:Oliver Dragojević.teaser: The singer a whole coast followed to sea: Split to Vela Luka by boat, July 2018
listening:Oliver Dragojević.story: Oliver Dragojević was born in Split in December 1947 and grew up in Vela Luka on Korčula, and for half a century his husky, unhurried voice was the sound of the Dalmatian coast: klapa harmony underneath, a jazz shadow on top. When he died in Split on 29 July 2018, his friends carried the coffin along the Riva while the crowd sang his songs; a catamaran took him home to Vela Luka escorted by two navy ships and hundreds of small boats, people on the docks holding torches and clapping. At the graveside in the Sveti Roko cemetery, Stjepan Hauser of 2CELLOS played Galeb i ja.
listening:Oliver Dragojević.why: Put Cesarica on during prep: every Croatian crew member will be singing by the second verse.
facts: Split, 7 December 1947; raised in Vela Luka, Korčula. Died Split, 29 July 2018
His grave is in the Sveti Roko cemetery at Vela Luka, on Korčula, a sail from Dubrovnik past Mljet
Queue Cesarica (1993, written for him by Gibonni), Galeb i ja, and the album Vridilo je, listed by the old guide as 2009

listening:Gibonni.name: Gibonni
listening:Gibonni.teaser: The Split songwriter who wrote Cesarica, then gave many of his Porin statuettes away
listening:Gibonni.story: Zlatan Stipišić, Gibonni, was born in Split in August 1968 and sings in the Dalmatian dialect over rock and pop arrangements that never lose the klapa line underneath. He is the reason Cesarica exists: he wrote it in 1993 for Oliver Dragojević, and the two names now open most Dalmatian playlists. He has won Croatia's Porin music award more often than almost anyone, five in a single night when Tolerancija was album of the year. In a 2021 interview he said the Porin site credited him with 37 and he doubted they were all his; he had handed many statuettes on to the musicians he thought had earned them.
listening:Gibonni.why: Libar is the track for the galley at closing time: slow, Dalmatian and wry.
facts: Split is his city and his summer stages are mostly up the coast; check the Dubrovnik Summer Festival programme for a rare appearance
Libar, Činim pravu stvar, Tek je 12 sati; the album Tolerancija; and Cesarica in Oliver's voice

listening:Klapa Cambi.name: Klapa Cambi
listening:Klapa Cambi.teaser: Tight, polished modern klapa from the Kaštela shore, and a long run of wins at Omiš
listening:Klapa Cambi.story: Klapa Cambi take their name from Kaštel Kambelovac, one of the seven seaside villages strung along the bay between Split and Trogir. They first sang at the Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa in 1991 and went on to a run of victories there, plus ten Porin awards, which is why Croatian press calls them the most decorated klapa there is. Their sound is the modern one: arranged, recorded, every vowel matched, the bass voices dropping under the first tenor like a floor. Put them on after a night of live street klapa and you hear the same tradition polished for the studio.
listening:Klapa Cambi.why: Moj lipi anđele is the track to start with; then compare a raw live klapa in the Old Town.
facts: Kaštel Kambelovac, near Split; first at Omiš in 1991
The Omiš Festival, mid-July to mid-August, has its own card under the calendar; Kaštela is on the drive from Split airport
Moj lipi anđele; then Klapa Iskon and Klapa Maslina, named by the old guide; Dubrovnik's own Klapa Kaše took the Omiš Golden Shield at the 60th festival

around:Cavtat.name: Cavtat
around:Cavtat.teaser: A pine-dark peninsula, a painter's birthplace and a white marble tomb at the very top
around:Cavtat.story: Cavtat sits on a double bay south of the airport, the old Epidaurum whose refugees are said to have founded Dubrovnik. Walk the palm-lined harbour to Bukovčeva street and the house where Vlaho Bukovac, the painter, was born in 1855; his studio and early pictures are inside. Then climb through the pines of the Rat peninsula to the cemetery at the top, where Ivan Meštrović built the Račić family mausoleum in 1920-22, a domed chapel of pale Brač stone with carved angels and a bronze bell, for a shipowning family that lost its son to the Spanish flu. The view runs back across the bay to the city.
around:Cavtat.why: The Meštrović mausoleum at the crown of the peninsula: quiet, cool and the best sculpture on this coast.
facts: About 17 km south-east by car (about 30 min), or by tender; the passenger boats from the Old Port run in season only, so check before November
The Račić mausoleum by Ivan Meštrović (1920-22) and Kuća Bukovac, Bukovčeva 5; the house's 2026 hours were not published, listings conflict, so check with Muzeji i galerije Konavala
No kept table in Cavtat itself; Konoba Konavoski Dvori on the Ljuta, inland in Konavle, has its own card

around:Sokol Grad.name: Sokol Grad
around:Sokol Grad.teaser: The Republic's falcon fort, grown out of a limestone crag at the Konavle frontier
around:Sokol Grad.story: Sokol grows out of a rock above Dunave, high in Konavle; it is hard to see where cliff ends and masonry begins. Bronze Age, Roman and Byzantine finds show the rock was held long before Ragusa. It is named in 1373, passed to the Republic with the Sanković donation of Konavle in 1391, and from about 1420 the Ragusans rebuilt and armed it as their watch on the inland border. Why it emptied is argued: the 1667 earthquake, 1672, or the Cretan War. The Society of Friends of Dubrovnik Antiquities took on the ruin in 1970 and opened it to visitors in 2013.
around:Sokol Grad.why: Climb to the top terrace: all of Konavle, and the borders beyond, laid out below you.
facts: Dunave, upper Konavle, about 40 minutes by car south-east of Dubrovnik
Listed as 10:00-19:00 June to October, 10:00-16:00 in November, 12:00-15:00 December to March (undated listing, seen Oct 2026); the old guide gave Nov-Mar 10:00-14:00. Call ahead in winter
EUR 8 (seen May 2026); no 2026 euro price found online
About an hour, longer with the small museum of finds

around:Trsteno Arboretum.name: Trsteno Arboretum
around:Trsteno Arboretum.teaser: A Ragusan noble's summer garden from the 1490s, survivor of shells and a wildfire, above a tiny harbour
around:Trsteno Arboretum.story: Ivan Marinov Gučetić began the summer villa and garden at Trsteno in 1494, and his family, the Gozze, kept adding to it for four centuries: Renaissance beds, a pergola walk, a baroque grotto and Neptune fountain. Ragusan captains brought seeds home. In 1948 Vito Gozze gave the estate to the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts. In early October 1991 shelling from the sea set much of it alight, and in the drought summer of 2000 a forest fire burned some 120,000 square metres. Two giant oriental planes in the village square, said to be over 500 years old, survived both.
around:Trsteno Arboretum.why: The two plane trees in the village square, then the cliff path down to the little harbour.
facts: About 15 km north-west along the coast road; by car, or the Libertas suburban bus from Gruž (check its timetable)

The two plane trees in the village, the Neptune fountain and grotto, and the old Gučetić villa; 2026 winter hours listed as 08:00-16:00 November to April, adults about EUR 10 (Oct 2026, from visitor guides, not HAZU)

around:Mljet.name: Mljet
around:Mljet.teaser: Two saltwater lakes in a pine forest, and a monastery on an islet in the middle of one
around:Mljet.story: The western end of Mljet has been a national park since 1960, pine and holm oak running down to two lakes that are not lakes: Veliko and Malo jezero are drowned karst basins, filled by the sea through a narrow channel, salty and still. On a small island in the larger lake stands St Mary's, a Benedictine monastery and church first built in the 12th century; a park boat takes you across. Walk the lakeshore path between the two lakes, swim off the flat rocks at the little bridge, and listen: out of season you mostly hear cicadas, oars and the occasional ferry horn from Polače.
around:Mljet.why: Take the boat to St Mary's islet, then walk the shore path back with a swim at the bridge.
facts: TP Line catamaran 9807 from Gruž via Šipan to Sobra and Polače; Polače is a conditional stop, and the winter timetable does not allow a same-day return, so out of season go by yacht or tender to Polače

The islet of St Mary in Veliko jezero: the park ticket includes a return boat; the 2026 price list exists (set Oct 2025) but we could not read the figures, and the boat may not run in winter: ask the park
